observations.title: Orano Enrichment USA, LLC; Uranium Enrichment Facility; Draft Environmental Impact Statement

data.abstract: The U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) is issuing for public comment a draft Environmental Impact Statement (EIS) regarding a license application from Orano Enrichment USA, LLC (Orano) to construct and operate a gaseous centrifuge uranium enrichment facility in Roane County, Tennessee. The draft EIS evaluates the environmental impacts of the proposed action of issuing a license that would authorize Orano to construct and operate a uranium enrichment facility on a 624-acre site, 6.7 miles southwest of Oak Ridge, Tennessee. The environmental impacts of the no-action alternative (i.e., denying the license application) are also evaluated.

observations.title: Airworthiness Directives; The Boeing Company Airplanes

data.abstract: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain The Boeing Company Model 707 airplanes; Model 720 and 720B series airplanes; Model 727C, 727-100, -100C, -200, and -200F series airplanes; and Model 747-100, -100B, -100B SUD, -200B, -200C, -200F, - 300, 747SR, and 747SP series airplanes. This proposed AD was prompted by reports that using some adaptors while performing tests of the cabin altitude warning switch (CAWS) could lead to incorrect failures. This proposed AD would require repetitive operational tests or replacements of the CAWS and applicable on-condition actions. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

data.abstract: The Board partially grants a petition for rulemaking and proposes amendments to its regulations implementing section 208 of the National Trails System Act Amendments of 1983 to streamline the railbanking process. Under the proposal, the Board would no longer issue Notices or Certificates of Interim Trail Use during trail-use negotiations. Only after an agreement is reached would the Board issue an order authorizing transfer to the trail sponsor. Abandonment authority would no longer be prerequisite to railbanking. The Board would also confirm that by authorizing transfer the Board is not exercising any power of eminent domain or authorizing a taking.

observations.title: Supervisory Committee Audits And Verifications

data.abstract: The NCUA Board (Board) is amending its regulations governing supervisory committee audits to eliminate unnecessary, redundant, and overly prescriptive provisions. The final rule is necessary to reduce regulatory burden, increase operational flexibility for federally insured credit unions (FICUs), and streamline the rules by removing requirements that are outdated or duplicative of other authorities. The intended effect of the final rule is to simplify compliance for FICUs without compromising the integrity of the audit process.

observations.title: Corporate Credit Unions

data.abstract: The NCUA Board (Board) is amending its regulations for corporate credit unions by removing the requirement that a corporate credit union's asset and liability management committee (ALCO) must have at least one member who is also a member of the corporate credit union's board of directors. The final rule also removes filing requirements related to a corporate credit union's annual report and any management letter or other report issued by its independent public accountant. The intended effect is to reduce unnecessary regulatory burden and provide corporate credit unions with greater flexibility.

observations.title: Thresholds Increase for the Major Assets Prohibition of the Depository Institution Management Interlocks Act Rule

data.abstract: The NCUA Board (Board) is issuing a final rule increasing two thresholds in its regulation implementing management official interlocks for purposes of the Depository Institution Management Interlocks Act (DIMIA). DIMIA authorizes NCUA to adjust the major assets prohibition thresholds through regulation to respond to inflation or market changes. This final rule increases both major assets prohibition thresholds to $10 billion to account for changes in the United States banking market since 1996. Additionally, the final rule removes a presumption related to depository institutions controlled or managed by persons who are members of a minority group or women.

observations.title: Airworthiness Directives; Airbus SAS Airplanes

data.abstract: The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2024-19-04, which applies to all Airbus SAS Model A350-941 and -1041 airplanes. AD 2024-19-04 requires a one-time detailed inspection of the engine nacelle anti-icing (NAI) forward bulkhead locating holes for elongation and loose fasteners and applicable corrective actions and prohibits the installation of affected parts under certain conditions. Since the FAA issued AD 2024-19-04, it has been determined that affected parts must accumulate at least 2,000 flight cycles (FC) since installation prior to the inspection to ensure that the inspection will detect discrepancies. This proposed AD would continue to require the actions in AD 2024-19-04 and would amend the compliance time for the inspection. This proposed AD would also prohibit the installation of affected parts under certain conditions. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

Loyalty and the Exclusive Purpose Rule in Selecting Plan Investments and Exercising Shareholder Rights

data.abstract: In this proposed rule, the Department of Labor (Department) clarifies the fiduciary duty of loyalty under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974 (ERISA). The proposed rule affirms that ERISA's duty of loyalty requires fiduciaries to act with the exclusive purpose of ensuring retirement security and providing promised benefits to plan participants and their beneficiaries. The amendments clarify the neutral application of ERISA's fiduciary duties of prudence and loyalty to selecting investments and investment courses of action, and to exercising shareholder rights, including proxy voting, the use of written proxy voting policies and guidelines, and shareholder engagement activities. The amendments would enhance the regulation by adding an affirmative expression of the duty of loyalty that is more consistent with the statute, and removing the tiebreaker test and participant preference provisions, which do not comport with the best reading of the statute and are susceptible to abuse, including use by a fiduciary as pretext to employ plan assets to pursue personal preferences or objectives unrelated to financial benefits under the plan. In the Department's view, the best reading of ERISA's exclusive purpose provision is and has always been that a plan fiduciary may not start with an ulterior motive or consider any factors collateral to plan participants' financial interests during any part of the process of making investment-selection decisions. The proposal would strengthen the fiduciary standards of pension and retirement plans covered by ERISA as instructed in President Trump's Executive Order 14366, Protecting American Investors from Foreign-Owned and Politically Motivated Proxy Advisors.
